# External data provenance and regeneration

The files in this directory are frozen fixtures and precomputed documentation
artifacts. `pepVet` never downloads data while it is installed, loaded, or
checked. This document identifies the original inputs and the repository
scripts used to create derived files.

The generation scripts are maintained in the
[`data-raw/`](https://github.com/LangeLab/pepVet/tree/main/data-raw)
directory of the source repository. Run them from the repository root in the
order described below. They intentionally are not run during package
installation or checking.

## UniProtKB FASTA fixtures

The top-level FASTA fixtures are frozen UniProtKB records:

| File | UniProtKB content |
| --- | --- |
| `P00698.fasta` | Chicken lysozyme C, accession P00698 |
| `P02769.fasta` | Bovine serum albumin, accession P02769 |
| `P0CG48.fasta` | Human polyubiquitin-C, accession P0CG48 |
| `P37840_isoforms.fasta` | Human alpha-synuclein canonical sequence and isoforms |
| `P56817.fasta` | Human beta-secretase 1, accession P56817 |
| `P68431.fasta` | Human histone H3.1, accession P68431 |
| `Q8WZ42.fasta` | Human titin, accession Q8WZ42 |
| `small_proteome_50_proteins.fasta` | A fixed panel of 50 human UniProtKB records |

The single-record files can be refreshed from the UniProt REST API by replacing
the accession in this example:

```sh
curl -L "https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02769.fasta" \
  -o inst/extdata/P02769.fasta
```

For `P37840_isoforms.fasta`, request the canonical P37840 entry together with
its isoforms from UniProtKB. The 50 accessions in
`small_proteome_50_proteins.fasta` are recorded in its FASTA headers and pinned
by `tests/testthat/test-reference-fastas.R`.

The original retrieval date and UniProt release were not recorded. The
committed files, rather than a current UniProt response, define the test
fixtures. When refreshing them, review sequence or header changes and update
the pinned accessions and widths in `tests/testthat/test-reference-fastas.R`.

## Tool-comparison data

`tool-data/` contains raw captures and derived tables for the comparison
vignette.

The two retained external raw captures use the P02769 sequence, trypsin, and
one allowed missed cleavage:

- `msdigest-bsa-trypsin.csv` is a tabular result exported from
  [UCSF ProteinProspector MS-Digest](https://prospector.ucsf.edu/prospector/html/instruct/digestman.htm).
- `expasy-bsa-trypsin.html` is an HTML result saved from
  [ExPASy PeptideMass](https://web.expasy.org/peptide_mass/).

Their service versions and retrieval dates were not recorded, so they are
retained as historical comparison inputs rather than current-service
benchmarks.

Run the following script after placing those two raw captures in `tool-data/`:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/fetch-external-data.R
```

It parses or creates:

- `tool-compare-msdigest.csv`
- `tool-compare-expasy.csv`
- `pepvet-bsa-trypsin.csv`

The PeptideRanger CSV files contain precomputed predictions made with
`PeptideRanger::RFmodel_ProteomicsDB`. Regenerating PeptideRanger-derived
comparisons requires PeptideRanger and its model data.

## Comparison-vignette tables

Run:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/full-tool-comparison.R
```

This creates the CSV files under `comparison-data/` from the frozen FASTA
fixtures, parsed tool outputs, pepVet results, documented tool capabilities,
PeptideRanger predictions, and the Protein Cleaver rules represented in that
script. The Protein Cleaver source revision used for the historical comparison
was not recorded; the retained table therefore describes the assessed
implementation and is not a current-version benchmark.

`data-raw/build-vignette-data.R` creates additional intermediate RDS files used
during documentation development. The shipped comparison vignette reads the
CSV files under `comparison-data/` directly.

## PeptideAtlas concordance artifacts

The files under `peptideatlas-concordance/` are generated by:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/peptideatlas-concordance.R
```

The script expects these large source files, which are not distributed in the
package:

- `scratch/peptideatlas-human-2026-01.fasta`: observed human peptides from the
  January 2026 PeptideAtlas build.
- `scratch/human-ref.fasta`: the UniProt human reference proteome used for the
  analysis.

The script fixes the random seed, samples 500 eligible reference proteins,
performs the concordance and parameter-grid analyses, and writes matching CSV
and RDS results. The exact input FASTA snapshots must be supplied to reproduce
the committed numerical values.

## Amino-acid property data

The installed `data/aa_properties.rda` dataset is created separately by:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/aa_properties.R
```

Its literature and database sources are documented in `R/aa_properties.R` and
the installed `?aa_properties` help page.
